parole.significato: file (block of coarse metal attached to a handle, used for removing sharp edges or cutting)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German vīle, or Middle Dutch vīle (“file”) (compare German Feile, English file). First mentioned in 17th-century sources.

parole.significato: doctor, physician (a specialist with a medical education who treats patients)
parole.testo: First mentioned in 16th-century translations, borrowed from Middle High German arste or Middle Dutch aerste, both derived from Vulgar Latin archiāter, from Ancient Greek ἀρχιατρός (arkhiatrós, “chief physician”).

parole.significato: dish, plate (round, rarely oval, usually flat bowl for serving food; its contents)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German schive (“disk, round plate, dish”), or maybe from Middle Dutch schijf or an East Frisian word (compare Saterland Frisian Schieuwe, Skieuwe; also compare German Scheibe).
